subsystems.name: Platform and hull
subsystems.role: gives the rocket a stable, level deck far out at sea.

subsystems.name: Station-keeping
subsystems.role: holds the platform within metres of the chosen launch point or landing target.

subsystems.name: Launch support structure
subsystems.role: carries, erects and releases the vehicle.

subsystems.name: Propellant and fluid handling
subsystems.role: stores and delivers cryogenic and storable propellants on a moving deck.

subsystems.name: Command, telemetry and range safety
subsystems.role: tracks the rocket and can destroy it if it goes off course.

subsystems.name: Marine logistics and recovery outfitting
subsystems.role: gets the platform to sea, keeps the crew safe and secures returning boosters.

buildSteps.title: Pick the site
buildSteps.detail: Choose equatorial or low-latitude water with mild sea states, clear of shipping lanes, and within a few days' tow of a port that can handle rocket hardware.

buildSteps.title: Select and convert the platform
buildSteps.detail: A semi-submersible gives the least deck motion, a barge is cheaper; either way the deck is reinforced for launch loads and fitted with ballast tanks to trim it level.

buildSteps.title: Build the launch mount
buildSteps.detail: A launch table with hold-down clamps and a flame path to the water is welded to the deck, with an erector to raise the vehicle and a conditioned enclosure to protect it from salt air.

buildSteps.title: Install propellant plant
buildSteps.detail: Insulated tanks, cryogenic pumps and vent masts are fitted; lines are routed with hazard zoning, gas detection and deluge so that a leak never reaches an ignition source.

buildSteps.title: Fit station-keeping
buildSteps.detail: Thrusters with dynamic positioning, or a mooring spread, are installed along with sensors that let the crew hold position and abort if motion exceeds launch limits.

buildSteps.title: Add range and comms
buildSteps.detail: Radar and satellite tracking, a flight-termination system, and a high-bandwidth link to mission control are installed and range-tested with a simulated launch.

buildSteps.title: Load out and transit
buildSteps.detail: The rocket is integrated horizontally or vertically at port, then the platform transits or is towed to the launch point under a weather forecast window.

buildSteps.title: Launch
buildSteps.detail: The deck is ballasted level, non-essential crew leave for a stand-off distance, propellants are loaded, and the vehicle lifts off with an empty ocean downrange.

buildSteps.title: Recover
buildSteps.detail: For reusable boosters, a landing deck with blast shielding catches the stage; securing hardware locks it down and the platform returns to port for refurbishment.

prerequisites.tech: Offshore dynamic positioning and semi-submersible vessels
prerequisites.why: the oil and gas industry already keeps large platforms fixed over a point in deep water.
proven by Sea Launch, which fuelled kerosene/LOX vehicles on a converted rig in the Pacific from 1999.

prerequisites.tech: Precision autonomous landing on a moving deck
prerequisites.why: demonstrated by reusable boosters since 2015, but still sensitive to sea state and only at a handful of sites.

prerequisites.tech: Satellite telemetry and autonomous flight safety
prerequisites.why: lets a platform launch far from land-based radars and still meet range-safety rules.

prerequisites.tech: Weather and sea-state forecasting at the launch point
prerequisites.why: deck motion and wave height set hard limits on when a launch or landing can be attempted.

pathway.milestone: converted rigs and barges launch small and medium rockets from the equator, and drone ships catch returning boosters
pathway.unlocks: flexible azimuths, equatorial performance gains of roughly 50–60 m/s over mid-latitude sites, and downrange water instead of land.

pathway.milestone: purpose-built self-propelled platforms with higher launch cadence
pathway.unlocks: shorter turnaround and operation from ports with no permanent launch site.
reuse cycles where the booster never needs a separate recovery ship.
refuelling at sea and, in theory, vehicles that leave from the ocean with more energy than a ground-launched equivalent.
